scale.basis: Plate18 caption explicitly gives specimen diameter220mm. Lateral width/height and ventral breadth estimated visually from the same published photos: width about0.85D, total thickness about0.28–0.30D. These secondary measurements are approximate, not caliper measurements.
scale.uncertainty: About10–15% for photo-derived proportions; retain actual moderately compressed lenticular fossil instead of artificially thinning to satisfy an adjective.

morphology: Strongly involute shell with one dominant broad outer whorl, small recessed umbilicus and nearly hidden early coils. Not an open coil, torus, or multiple exposed equal rings.

Planar coiling. Lateral silhouette is slightly oval rather than a perfect circle. Preserve the terminal opening in the outline at upper-left in Plate17: a distinct end of the whorl, not a closed seamless disk.

Flanks are broad and gently convex, converging toward a narrow ventral rim. The preserved rim is worn and blunt, with a subtle angular/flattened shoulder, not a razor blade, tall keel or tubular round edge.
Axial maximum thickness about63mm for220mm diameter, tapering strongly toward the periphery. Do not confuse the ventral face width with maximum flank thickness. No arbitrary uniform extrusion.
Umbilicus is a small stone-lined depression, not a cylindrical through-hole. Keep the umbilical wall and subtle overlap of the preceding whorl. No invented widely exposed spiral.

Subdued irregular falcate folds and weak rounded nodes occur on the outer flank, especially right side of Plate17; simplify without turning into heavy uniform ribs. Fine cracks are preservational and need not be copied.

The terminal face is mineral-filled/broken fossil, not a pristine thin hollow living aperture. Plate18 fig3 defines the irregular infilled terminal cross-section. Do not add a black tunnel or deep open mouth.
No ammonite body, eyes, tentacles, polished ammolite rainbow, cutaway chambers, museum labels, stand or slab. Matte stone appearance is an artistic choice.
uncertainty: Original genus-level target is fulfilled by a named complete fossil specimen interpretation, not a living reconstruction. Preserve damaged lip boundary; do not restore missing shell.
The original narrow angular rim is represented by real blunt-edged convergent geometry, without exaggerating it into a knife edge.

Opposite lateral surface is not directly photographed here; infer approximate bilateral shell symmetry conservatively, without inventing different anatomy or repeating damage as exact bilateral features.
No precise suture reconstruction or trace of unobserved inner chambers. Mineral-filled terminal face and shallow umbilical recess only.
palette: Matte neutral warm grey limestone; minimal material variation, no source-image textures.
acceptance_focus: Front comparison to Plate17: dominant involute whorl, small umbilicus, oval disk and terminal outline at upper-left.
Side/top: lenticular compression and narrow blunt angular rim, no rounded sausage edge or uniform flat extrusion.
Perspective: continuous single shell growth and visible infilled terminal boundary; no separate rings or invented hollow aperture.
Same specimen Plate17 and18 figs2–3 only, not P.pingue figure1. Four final views, independent QA judges original target match. Prep is not scientific PASS.
